proposed_widenings.name: species_trait_record
proposed_widenings.justification: No UnitRecord kind exists for species traits. types.ts defines SpellRecord, ClassFeatureRecord, and MasteryRecord only. The v4 taxonomy has species_trait_root as a source atom but the surface has no corresponding record family to host it.
proposed_widenings.evidence: Otherworldly Presence is a species_trait (kind: species_trait per the survey metadata), but UnitRecord = SpellRecord | ClassFeatureRecord | MasteryRecord — no species_trait branch exists.

proposed_widenings.name: grant_spell_access mechanic for species traits
proposed_widenings.justification: The core mechanic is a passive permanent grant of cantrip knowledge (Thaumaturgy). The v4 atom grant_spell_access exists but there is no surface type in ClassFeatureMechanics or any other mechanics family that can carry a passive spell-access grant without a use-count resource and reset cadence. A species-trait mechanics family would need a passive-grant shape.

proposed_widenings.name: cross_trait_spellcasting_ability reference
proposed_widenings.justification: The spellcasting ability for this cantrip is not a fixed Ability value but a reference to whatever ability the player chose for Fiendish Legacy. No existing surface type models a spellcasting ability as a cross-trait reference — Ability is a closed enum (str|dex|con|int|wis|cha) with no indirection variant.
proposed_widenings.evidence: When you cast it with this trait, the spell uses the same spellcasting ability you use for your Fiendish Legacy trait.

notes: The blocking gap is structural: no species_trait kind exists in UnitRecord. Forcing into class_feature would be dishonest — the unit has no className, no activation cost, no use-count resource, and no reset cadence. The mechanic is a passive permanent grant_spell_access. The secondary gap (cross-trait spellcasting ability) would require a surface_widening on top of the structural fix.
